agree.reason: This owner pays her cousin $600 a year, so she will see $199 a month as about $2,400 a year. The page never makes the case for that gap, so she is likely to close the tab instead of booking the call.

honest.reason: Every figure comes from the brief, and the missed closing dates are disclosed openly. The only stretch is listing 'closed by the 10th' as a firm feature before softening it to a target later on.

works_the_facts.reason: Framing the two departures as salon sales works well. But it never states the annual cost, never presents 9 of 31 as nearly a third of clients, never frames the 3 misses against roughly 370 on-time closes, and never puts the $800 saving next to the price.

right_comparison.reason: Her real alternative is a once-a-year cleanup at tax time for $600. The page never describes that option, never compares it with monthly books, and never says what she gives up by staying with it.

qualification.reason: The deadline caveat gives a date and a count (3 misses), but it never says what happens to the client when a close is late. The 'target' wording also leaves the promise vague.

objections.reason: The two main objections go unanswered: why pay roughly four times what her cousin charges, and how to handle a family relationship she values. The page does handle the smaller 'one person' and availability concerns well.

fit.reason: The page is about 330 words and ends on a booking button as the brief asked. The price section repeats the included list almost word for word, which wastes space.
